requirements.statement: Architecture Evaluation consumes the canonical CCG Module and dependency facts to derive architecture and physical ownership views without owning or rebuilding contract resolution.
The ARCH-DEPENDENCY-001 evaluator deterministically reports cycles in the Module graph derived from required capabilities.
Fortress records its current declared model and accurately reports that it is not certified.

Fortress deterministically compiles its complete live Module Contract v2 ecosystem into the canonical provenance-preserving CCG with unique identities, compatible capabilities, effective constraints, verification topology, exact input digests, and explicit unsupported semantics.
The compiler loads canonical Module Contract v2 and recursively discovered containment into one schema-versioned CCG containing every supported semantic domain with precise source provenance.

The CCG deterministically derives dependency reachability, inverse consumers, inherited and implied constraints, conflict failures, guarantee support, and parent-local verification topology without implicit capability re-export or unsupported proof claims.
Canonical CCG serialization is UTF-8, LF-terminated, deterministically ordered, content-addressed outside its own bytes, repeatable, and equal to Fortress's committed self-CCG Info artifact.
The core loads schema-versioned operational project configuration and rejects invalid, duplicate, or unsafe repository observation exclusions.
The temporal change schema represents ordinary changes without requiring bootstrap-only packet provenance.
Repository observation emits deterministic sorted repository-relative file facts with byte size and SHA-256 content identity.
Observation rejects unsafe exclusion paths and applies explicit exclusions without converting observations into declarations.

A canonical repository snapshot deterministically binds the exact declared standard/project inputs, explicit observation policy, stable observed file inventory, engine interpretation version, and content fingerprints without wall-clock identity.
Snapshot creation rejects a repository whose included path set, byte sizes, or content digests change between two canonical observation passes.
Snapshot rule violations use one validated content-addressed finding contract and a deterministic global sort order.
The Snapshot Governance engine validates the exact standard bundle, executes only registered applicable evaluators, and distinguishes evaluated pass/fail results from unsupported rules.

ARCH-OWNERSHIP-001 deterministically assigns every governed observed file to exactly one physical Module territory and reports orphan, incompatible overlap, or missing explicit fixture claims while respecting observation exclusions.

TEST-TRACEABILITY-001 loads distributed requirement ownership, extracts deterministic snapshot-bound Rust test facts, and rejects missing, orphaned, stale, duplicate, cross-boundary, marker-mismatched, or infrastructure-counted evidence.

A repository audit loads the exact declared inputs, builds a stabilized content-addressed snapshot, requires loaded declaration bytes to match it, analyzes supported Rust test facts, and deterministically evaluates every implemented applicable snapshot rule without claiming certification.

REPO-MODULE-001 defines and deterministically evaluates the canonical recursive Module grammar, including root surfaces, mandatory README.md and contract.json, code/mods obligations, attribute flatness, bidirectional code/data/info/mods documentation presence, and filesystem naming.

REPO-DOCS-001 parses canonical Module Markdown structurally, validates typed Module contracts, and deterministically reconciles filesystem catalogs, child catalogs, relationship projections, and relative links without treating unsupported source-dependency inference as evaluated.

CONTRACT-COHERENCY-001 passes only when canonical CCG compilation succeeds, its supported semantic graph is coherent, provenance is complete, and README relationship projection agrees while explicitly unsupported semantic classes remain non-evidence.

TEST-BOUNDARY-001 deterministically enforces recursive parent-local Feature verification through exact Testing-child presence, Feature subjects, role restrictions, source placement, and ownership-aware requirement evidence without introducing unit, integration, or end-to-end filesystem taxonomies.
The core validates canonical stable Fortress entity and rule identities under STD-ID-001.
The draft registry exposes unique valid rule metadata without claiming a released edition.
Every registered schema and draft standard record parses, has unique identity, and agrees with the implemented registry.

The selected standard validates canonical rule implication and conflict metadata, permits satisfiable implication cycles, and rejects unknown, self-conflicting, or inherently unsatisfiable rule logic.
The core command registry exposes only unique, stable, implemented command contracts.
CLI dispatch renders discovery and returns non-success for unsupported commands.
The native process implements version and help entrypoints with stable failure semantics.

The native fortress audit command accepts an optional repository root, renders deterministic human or schema-versioned JSON output, succeeds only without evaluated violations, and rejects malformed project state or unsupported options.

The native fortress ccg command compiles the canonical repository semantic IR once, renders deterministic canonical JSON, returns non-success for incoherency or invalid state, and rejects unsupported formats without implying certification.
